mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 3% over two consecutive quarters signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 below -2% indicates a significant contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in UNRATE above 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which boosts wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in INDPRO below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST below their 6-month moving averages signals weakening housing and overall demand, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of co-triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in FEDFUNDS followed by a concurrent decline in PAYEMS over the next two months signals an overtightening cycle, which depresses both growth and employment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases > 0.75% in one month and PAYEMS declines > 0.3% in the following two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered overtightening episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in UNRATE above 3.5% combined with a decline in RSAFS below its 12-month moving average signals strong labor demand but weakening business investment, which compresses profit margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 3.5% for three months and RSAFS < 12M MA
regime_hint: strong labor market with weakening investment
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between rising CPIAUCSL and declining S&P 500 5-day forward returns, as elevated inflation increases discount rates and erodes real corporate earnings.
failure_condition: The correlation between CPIAUCSL increases and negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in out-of-sample tests.
